agent.problem: Card 1 gives no context that points specifically to rest rather than riches or glory. The baker must supply the unseen BSB wording of the promise, so this is a guess at the next word of the line rather than a blank whose meaning can be reasoned out from the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The opening clause, “Twice they say no,” retells the refusals in Jeremiah 6:16-17, but the card cites only Jeremiah 6:18-19. Its citation therefore does not cover every verse the card uses; the recap needs its verses included or removed.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The distractor “neighbors” makes “the fruit of their own neighbors” nonsensical and is not the same kind of answer as “schemes” and “prayers.” It leaves “schemes” standing out as the only plausible completion.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
